eyebrow: California statewide air-quality policy · US, Bay and SF health
program: Conditional whole-organization value of a $100,000 unrestricted gift

nutshell.headline: Cleaner fleet operation can improve population health. Added advocacy's effect on deployment is unmeasured.
nutshell.body: Central donor estimates are $1.24 billion per 10 US QALYs, $12.4 billion Bay and $124 billion SF. The favorable joint case is $811,000 US, $3.60 million Bay and $23.2 million SF; its net resource numerator is nine times the gift. This model finds no demonstrated bargain.
nutshell.whyItMayWork: Current CCA policy work supports charging infrastructure that could bring clean truck and bus operation forward. A matched CARB zero-emission substitution model supports the physical mechanism.
nutshell.whyWeAreCautious: The health-per-truck anchor is a coarse ratio from a historical forecast, not a measured marginal effect. Future decision influence, actual deployment, competing projects, cost and residence shares are judgments.
nutshell.recommendationBlocker: Conditional research; independently audited model. No verified extra decision capacity or project-level deployment/exposure counterfactual; no donation recommendation.

summary.label: Central donor cost / 10 QALYs
summary.detail: Same $100,000 gift: 0.0000080411 SF, 0.000080411 Bay and 0.000804110 US QALYs. All assumed in California; regional health is nested.

summary.label: Whole-gift boundary
summary.detail: 40% assigned to future charging-related capacity, 60% other portfolio work with unquantified health. All-in staff cost includes shared delivery operations.

summary.label: Recipient
summary.detail: Official general donation form and FY2024–25 Form 990 identify the recipient; not a current IRS-status audit or a restricted Bay offer.

summary.label: Central net resource numerator
summary.detail: Gift plus zero assumed net public resource difference and $10,000 net private resources. Separate target gross envelope $160,000 before subtracting alternative-project resources.

programSection.body: CCA's whole portfolio includes freight and vehicle policy, climate, monitoring and education. This model quantifies only hypothetical future charging-allocation and implementation capacity while retaining all gift costs. It does not credit a new gift for old policy passage or already submitted comments.

steps.title: Fund additional future capacity
steps.detail: 40% of the gift at $200,000 per all-in staff-year buys 0.2 nominal staff-years. Funding additionality discounts replacement of existing support.

steps.title: Change a distinct decision
steps.detail: Two opportunities per staff-year and 10% incremental change probability yield 0.02 expected changed decisions after 50% funding additionality. Probability already conditions on coalition work.

steps.title: Enable earlier clean operation
steps.detail: A nominal 100-vehicle project enables half its vehicles earlier; the alternative forgone supplies 25 equivalent clean vehicles. Charger installation alone is not a health outcome.

steps.title: Count finite net health
steps.detail: Only three earlier operating years after two years' delay count, followed by finite avoided-death survival. Displaced-project health remains lost if target deployment fails.

programSection.boundary: Target, displaced and independent-harm geographies are separate. Bay includes SF. Do not duplicate the same decision, vehicle operation or pollution-mediated death across CCA, SPUR, Brightline or other coalitions.

model.headline: Future net clean-vehicle years, not enacted-policy totals
model.body: The model's central result is 1.5 net earlier clean-vehicle years and 0.000225 avoided deaths before finite survival and event-time discounting. Every marginal input is a judgment; the historical regulatory study supplies a coarse matched health scale only.

equation.label: Whole-gift capacity and displacement bridge
equation.expression: Staff = gift × charging allocation / all-in staff-year cost. Changed decisions = staff × distinct opportunities × incremental CCA change probability × funding additionality. Regional Q = (target accelerated vehicles × target share − displaced equivalents × displaced share) × annual death prior × transfer × finite survival tail × discounted acceleration-year sum − independent harm × harm share.
equation.result: Central 0.2 staff-years → 0.02 expected changed decisions → 1 target and 0.5 displaced vehicle-equivalents → 0.000804110 California QALYs at gift.

inputs.label: Charging allocation / all-in staff-year cash
inputs.basis: Staff cost includes related research and shared operations; not employee salary or functional-accounting ratio. Entire $100,000 stays in numerator.

inputs.label: Distinct opportunities / incremental decision change
inputs.basis: Probability already measures added CCA effect conditional on coalitions and agencies. No second coalition-credit multiplier and no duplicate projects.

inputs.label: Financial additionality
inputs.basis: Whether added staff work occurs rather than replacing funding. Distinct from decision attribution.

inputs.label: Nominal vehicles / actual earlier clean operation
inputs.basis: No named project offer. Includes vehicle availability, utilization, attrition and already committed baseline deployment.

inputs.label: Alternative clean-vehicle-equivalent fraction
inputs.basis: Independent of target success. Alternative need not literally buy trucks; same finite health scale represents forgone project health.

inputs.label: Annual mortality / transfer factor
inputs.basis: 2019 CARB ACT Table V-3: 18 deaths in 2030; Figure IX-1 roughly 60,000 ZEVs. Ratio is not a measured marginal derivative. Transfer aggregates modern baseline, grid, duty-cycle, exposure and timing mismatch; no inspection proxy.

inputs.label: Acceleration window / start delay
inputs.basis: Count earlier operation only until no-gift adoption catches up. Events at year midpoints; 3% discount.

inputs.label: Utility / competing mortality / finite tail
inputs.basis: 3.962 central QALYs at event. Separate from operating window; no statistical-life dollar conversion or repeat survival credit.

inputs.label: Target and displaced Bay / SF shares
inputs.basis: Historical air-basin pattern is only loose context; not SF city data or a guaranteed nine-county exposure map. All modeled health assumed California residents.

inputs.label: Target / alternative real project costs
inputs.best: Public $2M / $2M; private net $1M / $0.5M per changed decision
inputs.basis: Net real inputs at gift date; transfers excluded, public-paid assets not charged again privately. Private amounts include capital timing, energy and maintenance savings.

inputs.label: Independent donor harm diagnostic
inputs.basis: Separate from lost alternative-project health; survives no staff activity and uses its own geographic partition.

model.uncertaintyBoundary: Scenarios are not confidence intervals and central is not a calibrated expected value. Failure to enable clean operation retains displaced-project harm. Null and negative health have no positive ratio. Favorable prices remain far above $100,000/10 QALYs without threshold tuning. Whole-organization unquantified benefits could change overall value.
model.fundingBoundary: Official general giving is available. Current work motivates prospective capacity but no specific marginal staffing offer or affected project is verified. Existing mandates, already adopted funding and other advocates form baseline; old ACT passage earns no new-gift credit. Zero central public net cost is an equal-real-cost reallocation assumption, not measured free public resources.

evidence.design: CCA primary CEC comment and commission participation record
evidence.result: July 8, 2026 CCA comment prioritizes cleaner heavy-duty infrastructure. August 28 CEC report lists CCA among many participants.
evidence.transfer: Supports actual current organizational work, not decision success, funding additionality or exclusive attribution.

evidence.design: CARB 2019 proposed Advanced Clean Trucks forecast
evidence.result: 18 annual avoided deaths in 2030 and visually approximately 60,000 ZEVs provide an order-of-magnitude annual health scale.
evidence.transfer: Not a current regulatory forecast, per-truck experiment or structural marginal derivative. Old baseline, geography, stock and health timing differ from new charging projects; explicit transfer factor does not resolve uncertainty.

evidence.result: Identifies infrastructure, purchasing, turnover and cost constraints on acceleration and possible local traffic burdens.
evidence.transfer: No measured charging-adoption elasticity. Actual clean operation and independent displaced alternative are required.

evidence.design: CCA FY2024–25 Form 990; visually checked pages 1 and 10
evidence.transfer: Reconciled accounting and recipient identity, not current marginal cost or health allocation. No second overhead penalty.

evidence.result: Primary caveat says two high-pollution months cannot be annualized.
evidence.transfer: Not used as the numerical anchor; no inspection/maintenance effect imported.

reservations: The central $124B SF estimate is a very uncertain partial-health result, not an assessment of every benefit of CCA.
No measured marginal decision effect, complete project cost, actual clean-operation increment or alternative-project health.
Historical mortality/fleet ratio is coarse and nonstructural. Current diesel standards, grid supply, fleet mix and epidemiological timing can materially alter it.
Bay/SF shares are separate analyst assumptions; statewide externalities may benefit nonclients, but geography must follow exposure.
Public and private costs are present-value real-input scenarios; transfers and overlapping assets must not be counted twice.
excludedBenefits: Other CCA education, monitoring, climate and policy health
Noise, collision, congestion and construction harms except displacement/independent-harm stresses
Climate effects outside the air-pollution death branch
Medical spending and general fiscal opportunity costs
